sentences.text:
JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 10312/2021 Vijay Singh S/o Dhan Singh, Aged About 66 Years, H.No. 1,
Panchbatti Colony, Ratanada, Jodhpur.
 ----Petitioner  Versus State, Through PP  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. B.S. Charan.

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Mukesh Trivedi, PP.
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 18/08/2023 This anticipatory bail application has been filed by the petitioner apprehending his arrest in connection with FIR No.319/2020 registered at Police Station Udaimandir, Jodhpur for the offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B IPC.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that a civil dispute is pending before the competent court with regard to the disputed land.

Learned counsel further submitted that the land in question had been purchased by one Vijay Singh Parihar who stated himself to be the beneficiary of the 'will'
executed by Kanhaiya Lal and one cross FIR has been lodged by Chhavari Devi wife of Kanhaiya Lal on 02.12.2020.
Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner has been falsely roped in a criminal case though the dispute between the parties is of civil nature.

Learned counsel submitted that co-accused Kuldeep Singh (SB Cr. Misc.
(2 of 3) [CRLMB-10312/2021] Bail Application No.15117/2021) has already been enlarged on regular bail by a coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 11.11.2021.

Learned counsel submitted that in view of the fact that no recovery is due to be made from the petitioner and the custodial interrogation is not necessitated, the petitioner deserves to granted indulgence of anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.
However, he was not in position to refute the fact that co-accused Kuldeep Singh has already been enlarged on regular bail by a coordinate Bench of this Court.

Attention of the Court was also drawn by the learned Public Prosecutor towards the factual report received by him from the Investigating Officer wherein, he has stated that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not required in the present case.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and upon a consideration of the arguments advanced at the bar, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner under Section 438 Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest of petitioner-Vijay Singh S/o Dhan Singh in connection with FIR No.319/2020 registered at Police Station Udaimandir, Jodhpur, the petitioner shall be released on bail; provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- each along with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer/S.H.O. on the following conditions :-
(3 of 3) [CRLMB-10312/2021]
(i). that the petitioner shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii). that the petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or any police officer; and (iii). that the petitioner shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 205-Tikam/-
